problem:

\[
\begin{align}
f'(x) &= \frac{1}{2} f(x)\quad\text{for all } x,\\
f(0) &= 1,\\
|f(x)| &\le 6\quad\text{for all } x \in [-3, 3],
\end{align}
\]
find the higher error bound of the approximation of \(f(2)\) using the 6th degree MacLaurin polynomial \(T_6(2)\).

# Finding the Upper Error Bound for $T_6(2)$

## Setting Up the Taylor Remainder

The 6th degree Maclaurin polynomial has the Lagrange remainder:

$$R_6(x) = \frac{f^{(7)}(\xi)}{7!}\,x^7, \quad \xi \text{ between } 0 \text{ and } x$$

## Computing the 7th Derivative

Since $f'(x) = \frac{1}{2}f(x)$, differentiating repeatedly gives:

$$f^{(n)}(x) = \left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^n f(x)$$

Therefore:

$$f^{(7)}(x) = \frac{1}{2^7}\,f(x) = \frac{f(x)}{128}$$

## Bounding the Remainder at $x = 2$

$$|R_6(2)| = \left|\frac{f^{(7)}(\xi)}{7!}\cdot 2^7\right| = \frac{|f^{(7)}(\xi)|}{5040}\cdot 128$$

Using the derivative formula and the given constraint $|f(\xi)| \le 6$ (valid since $\xi \in (0,2) \subset [-3,3]$):

$$|f^{(7)}(\xi)| = \frac{|f(\xi)|}{128} \le \frac{6}{128} = \frac{3}{64}$$

## Computing the Error Bound

$$|R_6(2)| \le \frac{3}{64}\cdot\frac{128}{5040} = \frac{3 \times 128}{64 \times 5040} = \frac{3 \times 2}{5040} = \frac{6}{5040} = \frac{1}{840}$$

## Result

$$\boxed{\dfrac{1}{840}}$$
